title: Grateful Dead Live at Alpine Valley Music Theatre on 1982-08-07

ai_review.summary: Crisp soundboard capture of an incendiary Alpine ’82 show featuring a smoking Wheel, blistering Let It Grow and a legendary China>Rider segue.
ai_review.review: The recording is a clean SBD that delivers crystal‑clear guitar, vocals and drums, with only minor mix quirks noted by a few reviewers. Musically the performance is electric – Jerry’s tone and vocals are described as “on fire,” the Wheel is called a “rosetta stone” of the era, and the China>Rider transition along with Let It Grow and Althea are highlighted as standout moments.

ai_rating.rationale: The vast majority of reviews (≈90%) award 5‑star ratings, praising both the show and the soundboard quality; only a handful note minor mix issues or Phil’s playing, keeping the overall weighted rating in the high‑four range.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Consistently described as crisp, clean and “crystalline” SBD; a few comments mention slight mix imbalance (e.g., Brent/Bobby vocals) but no major dropouts or distortion.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Want You (Rider)
show_quality.setlist_flow: The set is praised for its powerful second‑set flow, especially the seamless China>Rider transition and the high‑energy Wheel; the first set holds its own with strong openers and solid closers.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly lauded for “on fire” guitar tone, crisp leads and smoky vocals; described as rehearsed, precise and in the zone.
band_member_comments.Phil: Generally positive but one reviewer notes he sounds out of sync on several songs; otherwise his bass work is praised (e.g., “Phil bombs”).
band_member_comments.Bob: Mentioned for strong backing vocals during The Wheel and overall solid rhythm work.
band_member_comments.Keys: References to Brent and Bobby vocal mix issues; no specific praise or criticism of keyboard playing itself.
band_member_comments.Drums: Called one of the best drum performances, tight and driving throughout.
